title: The Lantern of Port Mahon
premise: In the winter of 1918, Xanthe Delacroix keeps the lantern at Port Mahon while the great storms batter the coast and the war grinds toward an armistice that may never be signed. When a half-drowned child is left at her door clutching a sealed packet of naval dispatches — evidence that a convoy was deliberately sacrificed — she must choose between the loyalty she owes the harbor community that sheltered her and the truth that could hang powerful men. Smuggling the packet past three military checkpoints, Xanthe discovers the child is the daughter of the officer who wrote the dispatches, and that her own late husband's name appears in them as a collaborator. At the final checkpoint on the eve of the armistice, Xanthe trades the evidence for the child's safety, then publishes it anyway through a printer's widow, ending the book with the truth loose in the world and Xanthe lighting the lantern one last time before surrendering the post she inherited and finally understanding what survival cost everyone.
about_author: Mirabel Quintana is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal shipping records from the First World War. She writes from a house within earshot of a working lighthouse, where she claims the fog signal dictates her sentence rhythm.

chapters.title: What the Sea Returns
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Establishing the rhythms of the lighthouse during the year of the great storms: oil, logbooks, grief for her husband Tomas lost at sea two winters past. She measures everything by what can be carried. Emotional beat: disciplined loneliness masking dread that the war will reach the harbor.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. During the worst storm of the season she finds a girl, perhaps eight, soaked and silent on the lighthouse steps, a wax-sealed packet sewn into her coat and a note reading 'forget this face.' Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness breaking through routine.

chapters.title: Instructions to Forget
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, with the child's fragmented memories surfacing. The girl won't speak her name; the packet resists opening until Xanthe steams the seal and reads naval dispatches describing a convoy left without escort. Emotional beat: the vertigo of knowing something lethal.

chapters.title: The Harbor That Kept Her
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Port Mahon's community — the fishwives, the harbormaster Brannoc who found her work after Tomas died — closes ranks around rumors of a missing officer's family. Xanthe realizes the child matches the description. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to pull against truth.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A garrison proclamation orders all outbound travelers searched before the armistice signing; three checkpoints now guard the coast road. The packet must reach a naval court contact in the city or vanish forever. Emotional beat: cold strategic fear.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Would Not Be Named
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: the child, Ilsa, in spare interior chapters. She remembers her father burning papers, a night boat, hands pushing her ashore. She begins to trust Xanthe through small rituals of the light. Emotional beat: trauma learning the shape of safety.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Debt
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Brannoc offers to hide Ilsa but demands the packet be destroyed — his son serves on the convoy's escort ship and survived only by deserting. Xanthe sees how many people have reasons to bury the truth. Emotional beat: the weight of other people's survival.

chapters.title: Tomas's Name
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Reading deeper into the dispatches, she finds her husband listed among pilots who guided the convoy into the trap — paid, or coerced. Her grief curdles into betrayal. Emotional beat: the ground of memory giving way.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Disguising the run to the city as an oil-and-supply trip, she carries the packet inside a hollowed lamp reservoir, Ilsa posing as her niece. A suspicious sergeant nearly finds it. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into performance.

chapters.title: The Printer's Widow
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the city she seeks Court Clerk Aurel Vasse, but he has fled; instead she meets Odile Ferrand, a printer's widow who once ran contraband pamphlets. Odile offers another path: publish it. Emotional beat: temptation of a bolder, more dangerous truth.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Garrison Gate
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Returning through the gate, Ilsa recognizes the officer waving carts through — the man from the night boat. She freezes; Xanthe talks them past by invoking Brannoc's name. Emotional beat: the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Orders Come for the Light
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The navy requisitions the lighthouse as a signal station; keepers are to be displaced after the armistice. Her inheritance — the post, the life — has an expiration date. Emotional beat: loss compounding loss, sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Weighs
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Brannoc discovers she kept the packet and threatens to report her to protect his son. Their friendship fractures in the boathouse. Emotional beat: love and betrayal occupying the same hands.

chapters.title: The Armistice That Isn't
chapters.summary: Community chorus POV (harbor voices). Negotiations stall; rumors say the signing will fail and the war resume. Checkpoints tighten; executions of 'signal traitors' begin. Emotional beat: collective dread, the clock running down.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Quarantine Line
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The final checkpoint sits at the plague-quarantine arch where papers mean life. Odile arranges false transit documents, but they require a name — and Xanthe must decide whether to travel under Tomas's. Emotional beat: claiming a tainted inheritance.

chapters.title: The Face She Was Told to Forget
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The checkpoint officer is Ilsa's father's adjutant — alive, complicit, hunting the packet. He recognizes her. In a whispered exchange he offers to let them pass if the dispatches are surrendered. Emotional beat: a child offered safety at the price of silence.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Arch
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Climax begins: Xanthe hands over a decoy packet — Odile's forged duplicate — while the real pages ride sewn into Ilsa's coat, the one place no searcher would cut. They pass. Behind them, the adjutant opens the forgery. Emotional beat: desperate sleight of heart.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Hour
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Armistice terms are announced; guns fall silent at eleven. But the adjutant, humiliated, sends riders. Odile sets type through the night as the harbor waits. Emotional beat: breathless suspension between war's end and justice's beginning.

chapters.title: Ink Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The printing, the distribution by fish-cart at first light, the city waking to headlines naming the sacrificed convoy — and the pilots, including Tomas Delacroix. Emotional beat: truth escaping its cage, irreversible.

chapters.title: Reckoning at Port Mahon
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The adjutant is arrested; Brannoc, exposed as the informant who nearly doomed them, begs forgiveness. Xanthe neither absolves nor banishes him — she gives him the choice to testify about his son. Emotional beat: mercy as hard labor, not warmth.

chapters.title: The Last Firing of the Lamp
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The navy takes the lighthouse; Xanthe climbs the tower one final time with Ilsa, teaching her the lamp she lit through every storm. She leaves the logbook open on Tomas's page, unedited. Emotional beat: grief integrated, inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, closing frame. Years later, Ilsa — adopted, renamed, whole — visits the decommissioned light and carries out a single object: the original seal Xanthe kept. Some things are carried not despite their weight but because of it. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
